title: Controlled failover choreographer and latency-safe unwind
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary: Introduces a coordinated failover choreographer that sequences node drains, KV-cache safe handoffs, and per-tenant SLO fences to perform regional failovers and graceful degradation with bounded latency impact. Motivation: Recent incidents showed that parallel region failovers and uncoordinated kv-evacuation caused token spikes and client-visible latency regressions. This PR implements a staged choreography layer that reduces bursty reconnections and avoids violating tenant SLOs during emergency evacuations.

What this change does: Implements a small orchestration layer in the runtime scheduler that: 1) establishes an SLO 'harbor' window for affected tenants (timeboxed preserve of latency SLAs), 2) sequences KV cache preservation and handoff with a short-lived lease so slowpath clients are gracefully redirected, 3) limits concurrent node-drain operations via a global throttle and per-zone concurrency budget, 4) provides a telemetry contract surface (events: choreo.start, choreo.step, choreo.finish, choreo.abort) for observability and automated paging, 5) automatic rollback/fast-reopen if KV handoff fails within a detection window, and 6) optional emergency fast-path that preserves highest-priority tenant tokens by temporarily freezing lower-priority queues.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-7190), [x] unit + integration tests for choreography transitions, [x] end-to-end canary in perf-lab region, [x] console dashboard tiles for choreo events, [x] migration/rollout plan for Dedicated and Private.

Backwards compatibility and gating: The choreography is feature-flagged by config.runtime.failover_choreographer (off by default for existing clusters). When enabled, the system advertises the choreographer capability in node metadata so control-plane rollouts can be performed gradually. The default policy is conservative: 2 concurrent drains per zone, 30s KV handoff lease, 60s harbor window. These defaults can be tuned per deployment.

Testing and canary notes: Deployed to perf-canary (eu-west-1) for a 48h soak. Observed a 37% reduction in token replays and no SLO violations in the canary tenant cohort. CI: full unit suite + runtime integration on k8s overlay.

Deployment plan: Feature-flag rollout (canary -> staged regional ramp -> global), enable observability for 72h at each step, automatic rollback via console if choreo.abort rate > 0.5% over 10m.

Risks and mitigations: Risk: choreography can slow emergency evacuation if misconfigured; mitigation: default conservative timeboxes and an emergency 'fast-unwind' override for operator use. Risk: stale KV leases on network partitions; mitigation: TTL-based lease and fast reclaim path on disconnect.

Related work: builds on the KV-preserve mechanics introduced in ENG-6531 and integrates with the SLO-metering hooks from ENG-6822.
commit_summary: choreographer: add orchestration primitives and state machine
scheduler: wire choreographer into drain flow with permissive feature flag
kv: introduce handoff lease and safe-commit protocol
telemetry: emit choreo.* events and add prometheus metrics
console: add basic choreographer dashboard tiles (canary only)
tests: add state-transition unit tests and integration scenario harness
review_comments: Samir Patel: Can you confirm the failure modes for KV handoff? What happens to in-flight requests if the lease cannot be acquired?

Maya Chen (author): If the lease fails we trigger a fast-unwind: we stop additional drains, mark the node as quarantined, and increment a choreo.abort counter so operators are paged. In-flight requests are retried on the local node while quarantine is active to avoid mass replays.
Lina Gomez: Large change — please ensure the observability labels are present on all choreo.* events; we need team dashboards to filter by tenant and region.
Maya Chen (author): Added tenant and region labels to all event emissions in telemetry commit, updated dashboard definition.
Theo Rivera: Tests look good; can we add a targeted stress test that simulates N+1 region outage with slow network so we validate lease TTL reclaim behavior?
Maya Chen (author): Added an integration scenario in perf-lab that runs a slow-network simulation with lease TTL asserts; results included in canary notes.
release_notes: Introduce controlled failover choreographer (opt-in) to sequence node drains and KV handoffs with SLO-preserving windows. Feature gated; default conservative params. See docs/ops/failover_choreographer.md for rollout steps and tuning.
